claims.content: To complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing a checkout option and completing the transaction(s).

goal.raw_text: To complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing a checkout option and completing the transaction(s).

claims.content: Customer
The customer has won an auction.
The customer has unpaid auction winnings.
The customer’s registration data includes a default Method of Payment (MOP) of PayPal or Amazon Payments.
The customer has been identified via a cookie, the “pay now” link in the winner notification email from Responsys, or because they signed in.
The customer chooses a checkout option to complete their transaction(s) for won items.

trigger.raw_text: The customer chooses a checkout option to complete their transaction(s) for won items.

claims.content: The post-auction checkout page displays a congratulatory message: Congratulations! You've won XX items for a total of $XXX.XX. We've included a list of these items below.

The page states: You are seeing this message because you have chosen either PayPal or Amazon Payments as your default method of payment. Please complete your transaction(s) now by choosing a checkout option.
The final section is the Checkout Options section, which consists of three logo buttons, with a radio button next to each.
The user chooses a checkout option.

The selected checkout process is presented: clicking on the PayPal logo or radio button immediately takes the user to the PayPal checkout process, and the next page the user sees is a PayPal-hosted page; clicking on the Amazon Payments logo or radio button immediately loads the Amazon Payments checkout widget on the page, without leaving the page, while the page remains in the background, grayed out, and all other links are disabled, and the rest of the process is per the Amazon integration guidelines documentation.
The user completes the transaction(s) through the selected checkout process.
1. Clicking on the PayPal logo or radio button immediately takes the user to the PayPal checkout process; the next page the user sees is a PayPal-hosted page.

2. Clicking on the Amazon Payments logo or radio button immediately loads the Amazon Payments checkout widget on the page, without leaving the page; the page remains in the background, but grayed out, and all other links are disabled; the rest of the process is per the Amazon integration guidelines documentation.
3. Clicking on the “Checkout Later” button or radio button immediately grays out the page and disables all links; a DIV layer appears.

4. Orders won with an alternative payment method, i.e. PayPal or Amazon Payments, will be placed in a Hold status until payment is received; when an auction is won, the customer will be sent an email, requiring payment; if payment is not received within 168 hours, the item order will be cancelled.

1. If the customer selects “Checkout Later” instead of completing checkout, the page grays out and disables all links and a DIV layer appears; the DIV states that the customer can come back to pay anytime within 7 days (exactly 168 hours) after winning auction(s), that unpaid orders will be cancelled after the payment window expires, and that bidding incurs an obligation to pay when they win per the Terms of Use Agreement. Exit: the customer selects “Return to Payments” to close the DIV and re-enable page links, or selects “JTVauctions Homepage” to go to the home page.
2. If the customer does not pay within the payment window, any unpaid orders will be cancelled after the payment window expires. Exit: the unpaid order is cancelled.
The Amazon or PayPal checkout process has been completed.
The user is returned to a Thank You page.
Payment is received for the order(s) won with an alternative payment method, i.e. PayPal or Amazon Payments.
Payment is made within seven days (168 hours) of the auction’s closing date/time.
